# Cyberpsychology: Journal of Psychosocial Research on Cyberspace

> A peer-reviewed open-access journal publishing research on psychological and social aspects of internet use, online behavior, and digital technologies.

Cyberpsychology.eu is an international academic journal indexed in major databases that examines how digital environments shape human psychology, behavior, and social interactions. The journal covers emerging topics including AI applications, social media effects, cyberbullying, and online prosocial behavior across diverse populations.

## Key Topics

- cyberpsychology
- online behavior
- social media
- cyberbullying
- mental health
- social comparison
- anxiety
- empathy
- prosocial behavior
- internet research
- ChatGPT
- psychological analysis
- helping behavior
- open access
- peer review

## Journal Overview

- [Homepage](https://cyberpsychology.eu): Homepage for peer-reviewed open-access journal on cyberpsychology and internet research
- [About the Journal](https://cyberpsychology.eu/about): Journal overview covering indexing, ethics, editorial board, and publication standards

## Research Articles

- [Striving for accuracy attenuates the positive relationship between cyberbullying bystanders' dispositional empathy and tendencies to help victims](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/40683): Research article on cyberbullying bystander empathy and helping behavior by Liu et al.
- [The role of social norms for online prosocial & antisocial behavior among adolescents in Singapore](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/37092): Research article on social norms influencing adolescent online behavior in Singapore
- [Evaluating strengths, limitations, and future directions of ChatGPT in psychological analysis within case conceptualization: A qualitative analysis](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/40142): Research article evaluating ChatGPT's application in psychological case analysis
- [Decoding user disclosure intentions in generative AI: Exploring the influence of system attributes on trust and privacy concerns within the extended technology acceptance model](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/40364): Research article on user disclosure and privacy in generative AI systems
- [Caught in the daily scroll: How upward social comparison fuels daily anxiety during short video use among Chinese young adults](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/40189): Research article on social comparison and anxiety from short video use
- [When sadists become internet trolls: The mechanism of aggressive humor and self-concept clarity](https://cyberpsychology.eu/article/view/35694): Research article on sadism, aggressive humor, and internet trolling behavior
